messages:
helen: FYI alert: sudden nvme wear alerts in ap-northeast1 cohort -> scheduler started throttling GPU attaches. attaching short summary.
omar: How many nodes and what metric tripped?
helen: ~14 hosts. SMART wear_level jumped past our soft threshold (80%) on small-block counters, and janitor increased scrub intensity which amplified IO. pager-bot pasted: wear_rate_scale=1.8 -> throttle.
rui: Any signs of corruption? checksum errors?
helen: No hard corruption yet, but a few io-timeout spikes and increased retry rates from storage layer -> attach validation p95 inflated.
omar: Possible causes: recent background scrub cadence change + a firmware flash last week. Both could increase write amplification.
helen: Right — group had firmware 5.2 pushed two nights ago and scrub cadence was tightened in last config roll to reduce stale tempfiles. Combined effect > expected.
pager-bot: Auto-mitigation kicked: reduce scrub concurrency, enable wear-friendly mode on janitor for affected pool.
rui: Good. What about provisioning impact? numbers?
helen: Pending GPU attach backlog rose to ~2100, attach failures up 12% in the region. After auto-mitigation backlog dipped to 980 in 12m.
finance: Note: routing attaches away from ap-northeast1 will cause cross-region egress; estimated incremental cost ~¥0.20/hr for heavy workloads.
omar: Plan: 1) keep scrub concurrency lowered and enable wear-friendly janitor for 2h 2) roll firmware rollback for a small canary group if metrics don't improve 3) schedule a maintenance to rebalance scratch allocation away from hot stripes.
rui: Also add a short-term circuit: if wear_level > 85% then drain node for non-critical jobs and mark for replacement on next maintenance window.
helen: I'll open ops ticket and start a canary rebalance now. Also adding metric wear_spike_count and alert when >5 hosts in a region.
omar: Who owns follow-ups? helen will own the rollback decision; rui takes rebalance automation; finance flagged cost impact.
helen: Canary rebalance started on 3 nodes. Monitoring.
pager-bot: Incident recorded: INC-20260405-nvme-wear-flood. Assigned: helen/omar/rui.
